questions.stem: Independent trials each succeed with probability 0.40. Calculate the probability that the first success occurs on trial 5.
questions.solution:
For a geometric distribution, P(X=k) = (1-p)^(k-1) p.
P(X=5) = 0.60^4 x 0.40 = 0.129600 x 0.40 = 0.0518.

questions.stem: The lifetime of a component (in years) follows an exponential distribution with mean 10. Calculate the probability that the component lasts more than 2 year(s).
questions.solution:
For an exponential with mean theta, P(X > t) = e^(-t/theta).
P(X > 2) = e^(-2/10) = 0.8187.

questions.stem: A random variable X is uniformly distributed on the interval [5, 11]. Calculate the variance of X.
For events A and B, P(A and B) = 0.24 and P(B) = 0.60. Calculate P(A | B).
questions.solution:
By definition, P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B).
P(A|B) = 0.24 / 0.60 = 0.4000.

questions.stem: Machine A produces 50% of a factory's output with a defect rate of 4%. Machine B produces the remaining 50% with a defect rate of 12%. An item selected at random is found to be defective. Calculate the probability that it came from Machine A.
For events A and B, P(A) = 0.30, P(B) = 0.35, and P(A and B) = 0.10. Calculate P(A or B).
questions.solution:
By inclusion-exclusion, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).
P(A or B) = 0.30 + 0.35 - 0.10 = 0.550.

questions.stem: A discrete random variable X has the following distribution: P(X=1)=0.20, P(X=2)=0.30, P(X=4)=0.50. Calculate E[X].
For random variables X and Y, E[X] = 5, E[Y] = 4, and E[XY] = 21. Calculate Cov(X, Y).
questions.solution:
Cov(X, Y) = E[XY] - E[X]E[Y].
Cov(X, Y) = 21 - 5 x 4 = 1.00.

questions.stem: For random variables X and Y, Var(X) = 4, Var(Y) = 9, and Cov(X, Y) = 2. Calculate Var(X + Y).
questions.solution:
Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) + 2 Cov(X, Y).
Var(X + Y) = 4 + 9 + 2 x 2 = 17.00.
